✻ Worked for 2s · done 3:52 AM

❯ I want to restructure the trading system based on what we've learned from the 
  latest research.                                                              
                                                                                
  Do NOT simply loosen the liquidity filter.                                    
                                                                                
  I think we've discovered a deeper structural issue:                           
                                                                                
  The strategy is trying to find explosive low-float momentum stocks, while     
  also requiring enough liquidity for safe execution and eventually operating   
  with relatively small accounts.                                               
                                                                                
  Those objectives can conflict.                                                
                                                                                
  Think of the problem as a three-way tradeoff:                                 
                                                                                
  1. Large/explosive price movement                                             
  2. High liquidity / good execution                                            
  3. Small account / small risk                                                 
                                                                                
  We need to find the practical middle ground rather than blindly maximizing    
  any one of these.                                                             
                                                                                
  The most important change I want is to separate:                              
                                                                                
  SIGNAL QUALITY                                                                
                                                                                
  from                                                                          
                                                                                
  EXECUTION FEASIBILITY.                                                        
                                                                                
  ==================================================                            
  1. CREATE TWO DISTINCT LAYERS                                                 
  ==================================================                            
                                                                                
  The system should have two major stages:                                      
                                                                                
  STAGE A — SIGNAL ENGINE                                                       
                                                                                
  STAGE B — EXECUTION ENGINE                                                    
                                                                                
  The Signal Engine answers:                                                    
                                                                                
  "Is there a statistically interesting trading opportunity?"                   
                                                                                
  The Execution Engine answers:                                                 
                                                                                
  "Can we realistically trade this opportunity under our risk, liquidity,       
  spread, and position-size constraints?"                                       
                                                                                
  Do not allow the execution filter to erase the existence of the signal from   
  the research dataset.                                                         
                                                                                
  Example:                                                                      
                                                                                
  ARTL                                                                          
                                                                                
  Signal:                                                                       
  BEARISH                                                                       
                                                                                
  Signal quality:                                                               
  PASS                                                                          
                                                                                
  Liquidity:                                                                    
  FAIL                                                                          
                                                                                
  Spread:                                                                       
  PASS                                                                          
                                                                                
  Execution:                                                                    
  FAIL                                                                          
                                                                                
  Later price movement:                                                         
  -51.8%                                                                        
                                                                                
  The system should preserve ALL of this information.                           
                                                                                
  We need to know:                                                              
                                                                                
  "The signal was directionally correct, but execution was not feasible under   
  our current constraints."                                                     
                                                                                
  That is much more useful than simply recording:                               
                                                                                
  "ARTL rejected."                                                              
                                                                                
  ==================================================                            
  2. DO NOT CHANGE THE LIQUIDITY THRESHOLD YET                                  
  ==================================================                            
                                                                                
  The recent sample showed that liquidity was the dominant rejection reason.    
                                                                                
  However, we do NOT know yet whether:                                          
                                                                                
  A. The liquidity filter is correctly protecting us from bad execution         
                                                                                
  OR                                                                            
                                                                                
  B. The liquidity filter is unnecessarily eliminating potentially tradeable    
  opportunities.                                                                
                                                                                
  Do not guess.                                                                 
                                                                                
  Build the research infrastructure to answer this.                             
                                                                                
  ==================================================                            
  3. STOP USING RAW SHARE COUNT AS THE ONLY DEFINITION OF LIQUIDITY             
  ==================================================                            
                                                                                
  A 50,000-share threshold by itself is not enough.                             
                                                                                
  A stock trading 50,000 shares at $1 is very different from a stock trading    
  50,000 shares at $50.                                                         
                                                                                
  Record an                                                                     
  ──── (492 lines hidden) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── 
  % at 30 minutes.                                                              
                                                                                
  The bullish signals had X%...                                                 
                                                                                
  Liquidity accounted for X% of execution failures.                             
                                                                                
  Spread accounted for X%.                                                      
                                                                                
  Position sizing accounted for X%.                                             
                                                                                
  Shortability accounted for X%.                                                
                                                                                
  Estimated slippage accounted for X%."                                         
                                                                                
  That is the type of research output I want.                                   
                                                                                
  ==================================================                            
  19. DO NOT OPTIMIZE YET                                                       
                                                                                
  Do NOT:                                                                       
                                                                                
  - lower liquidity arbitrarily                                                 
  - remove filters because they reduce trade count                              
  - add filters because they improve one day's results                          
  - declare bearish superior                                                    
  - declare bullish broken                                                      
  - optimize thresholds on the current sample                                   
  - select parameters based on hindsight                                        
                                                                                
  The current findings are hypotheses.                                          
                                                                                
  The goal is to build the measurement system that can test those hypotheses.   
                                                                                
  ==================================================                            
  20. FINAL ARCHITECTURE                                                        
                                                                                
  I want the system conceptually structured like this:                          
                                                                                
                  MARKET DATA                                                   
                      ↓                                                         
               POINT-IN-TIME                                                    
                  REPLAY                                                        
                      ↓                                                         
               SIGNAL ENGINE                                                    
                      ↓                                                         
            ┌─────────┴─────────┐                                               
            ↓                   ↓                                               
         BULLISH             BEARISH                                            
            ↓                   ↓                                               
       Signal valid        Signal valid                                         
            │                   │                                               
            └─────────┬─────────┘                                               
                      ↓                                                         
               EXECUTION ENGINE                                                 
                      ↓                                                         
          ┌───────────┼───────────┐                                             
          ↓           ↓           ↓                                             
      Liquidity     Spread     Shortability                                     
          ↓           ↓           ↓                                             
          └───────────┼───────────┘                                             
                      ↓                                                         
               POSITION SIZE                                                    
                      ↓                                                         
               RISK / SLIPPAGE                                                  
                      ↓                                                         
              EXECUTABILITY                                                     
                      ↓                                                         
            REALISTIC BACKTEST                                                  
                      ↓                                                         
                 ANALYSIS                                                       
                                                                                
  The fundamental question we're trying to answer is no longer:                 
                                                                                
  "Can we find stocks that move?"                                               
                                                                                
  We already know we can.                                                       
                                                                                
  The question is:                                                              
                                                                                
  "Can we find statistically repeatable directional signals that can ALSO be    
  executed realistically at the account sizes we care about?"                   
                                                                                
  Build toward answering that question.

● Architecture Proposal

  Before touching code, one finding that reshapes this whole plan — I checked
  the actual source of today's "bearish" signals, and it's not what it looks
  like:

  Today's "bearish" signals aren't a real short screen — they're an accident.
  ross_strategy.evaluate() only has one gain pillar: percent_change >= 
  min_percent_gain (10%, positive). Candidates are sourced exclusively from
  top_gainer_symbols + most_active_symbols — there's no down-mover source at
  all. market_structure's break-of-structure detector is direction-agnostic and
  happens to also catch bearish (breakdown/reversal) patterns within that
  up-moving price action. So "ARTL: bearish" doesn't mean "we found a stock
  breaking down" — it means "a stock that spiked hard enough to pass an UP-only
  screen is now reversing." That's a real, tradeable idea (fade-the-spike), but
  it's not what item 8 is asking for, and it's not symmetric with the bullish
  side at all.

  Two more things I checked that materially change what's buildable:
  - Alpaca's screener does expose movers.losers (real down-movers) — verified
    live, currently completely unused.
  - Alpaca's TradingClient.get_asset() does expose live shortable/easy_to_borrow
    flags — verified live (ARTL is currently shortable: False, unborrowable,
    right now). But this is a current snapshot only — Alpaca has no historical
    point-in-time shortability API. For any backtested candidate, I cannot know
    if it was shortable at the time of the signal — only right now. Per your own
    instruction in item 7, every backtested record's shortability will be
    marked SHORTABILITY_UNKNOWN, not silently assumed. Only live/current-day
    checks can ever say SHORTABLE/NOT_SHORTABLE for real.

  1. Architecture (your diagram, mapped to real modules)

  scanner/ (existing, point-in-time already fixed)
          │
    ┌─────┴─────┐
    ↓           ↓
  ross_strategy/     bearish_strategy/  (NEW — mirrors ross_strategy's shape,
  (existing,           sourced from top_loser_symbols [NEW, wired to
  UP-only screen)       movers.losers] + most_active_symbols, its own
                        magnitude pillars: min_relative_volume +
                        min_percent_loss)
    │           │
    └─────┬─────┘
          ↓
  market_structure/ + icc_strategy/ (existing, already direction-agnostic —
                                      reused as-is for both directions)
          ↓
     signal.py (NEW, in backtesting/) — SignalRecord: SIGNAL_VALID,
     direction, full feature set (item 3), all 4 provenance timestamps (item 17)
          ↓
  execution/ (NEW package — liquidity tiers, participation rate, shortability,
              realistic fill simulation) — consumes risk_manager's existing
              execution_feasibility/account_state/sizing category split,
              extends it with tiers instead of pass/fail
          ↓
     TRADE_VALID classification + per-account-size executability (item 14)
          ↓
     outcome.py (NEW) — 1/5/15/30/60-min forward prices, MFE/MAE, regardless
     of executability
          ↓
     research narrative report (item 18's format)

  2. Files that need modification/creation

  New:
  - bearish_strategy/ — config.py, evaluator.py, models.py (mirrors
    ross_strategy/)
  - scanner/data_source.py — add top_loser_symbols() to ScannerDataSource (new
    abstract method, implemented via movers.losers)
  - execution/ — liquidity_tiers.py (Tier 1-4 classification, item 13),
    participation.py (position-size-vs-volume ratios, item 4), shortability.py
    (live-only check + SHORTABILITY_UNKNOWN for backtests, item 7),
    fill_simulation.py (spread/slippage-aware realistic entry, item 11),
    account_sim.py (multi-equity-size executability, item 14)
  - backtesting/signal.py — the SignalRecord/ExecutionRecord/TradeOutcome
    three-way model (item 6, 12)
  - backtesting/outcome.py — forward-price + MFE/MAE study (item 10)
  - backtesting/narrative.py — the human-readable research report generator
    (item 18)
  - Corresponding test files for every module above

  Modified:
  - risk_manager/models.py/engine.py — extend RiskCheck.category machinery to
    feed the new tier system rather than duplicate it
  - backtesting/runner.py — restructure into the two explicit stages (Signal
    Engine → Execution Engine) instead of one linear function
  - backtesting/universe.py — Universe A/B unaffected in shape, but Universe A's
    candidate sourcing gains the loser-symbol path for bearish
  - market_data/base.py — Quote already has bid/ask + sizes; no change needed
    there

  3. New data fields (on top of what the last overhaul already added — 
  data_quality, liquidity_bucket, signal_valid, execution_valid, 
  rejection_chain)

  - Provenance (item 17): data_timestamp, signal_timestamp, execution_timestamp
    — distinct fields, not one as_of reused three ways, so a future auditor can
    mechanically check none of them are out of order
  - Liquidity detail (item 3): already have volume/avg_volume/dollar_volume/rela
    tive_volume/spread/spread_percent/bid_size/ask_size/float from the last
    overhaul — adding execution_tier (1-4), participation_rate (position size ÷
    available volume, at multiple candidate position sizes)
  - Direction semantics (item 7): signal_direction (bullish/bearish — "candidate
    for," not "will execute"), shortability_status (SHORTABLE / NOT_SHORTABLE /
    SHORTABILITY_UNKNOWN)
  - Outcome (item 10): price_at_1m/5m/15m/30m/60m, mfe, mae (sign-aware per
    direction — down is favorable for bearish)
  - Small-account (item 14): a list of AccountSizeResult per candidate — one row
    per tested equity level, with shares/executable/reason

  4. New tests

  Every new module gets real tests following this codebase's established house
  style (fake data sources, no live network calls, pytest.approx), plus:
  - A dedicated provenance test: construct a signal where a "future" field is
    deliberately injected and assert the system either can't produce it or flags
    it — a mechanical proof, not just a docstring claim
  - A dedicated shortability test: prove a backtested (non-live) record can
    never come back SHORTABLE — only UNKNOWN or (for genuinely live calls) real
    values
  - A dedicated hypothesis-tracking test for item 9: confirm the system reports
    bullish vs. bearish outcome distributions side by side without ever emitting
    a "bearish is better" verdict anywhere in code or output

  5. Bullish signal definition

  Unchanged from what already exists and is tested: Ross's screen
  (relative_volume + percent_gain, both magnitude/up-only) → ICC bullish
  continuation. This is not being touched.

  6. Bearish signal definition

  New bearish_strategy.evaluate(), structurally mirroring Ross's (magnitude
  pillars: min_relative_volume, min_percent_loss), sourced from
  top_loser_symbols (new) + most_active_symbols, feeding the same
  market_structure/icc_strategy bearish-direction detection already in the
  codebase. Per your item 8 instruction, I will not hardcode
  VWAP-rejection/failed-breakout/exhaustion-reversal logic as a filter yet —
  those become recorded features on every signal (computed, stored, not filtered
  on), so a later pass can measure which ones actually correlate with favorable
  outcomes. Shipping a filter based on a list I made up would be exactly the
  hindsight-driven optimization item 19 forbids.

  7. Shortability representation

  shortability_status: Literal["SHORTABLE", "NOT_SHORTABLE", 
  "SHORTABILITY_UNKNOWN"]. Live calls (worker polling right now) hit
  TradingClient.get_asset() for a real answer. Any backtested record — which is
  inherently checking a past moment — is always SHORTABILITY_UNKNOWN, full stop,
  because no historical borrow API exists. This is enforced structurally (the
  backtest code path never calls the live shortability check), not by
  convention.

  8. Liquidity measurement

  All the fields already added in the last overhaul (volume, avg_volume,
  dollar_volume, relative_volume, spread, spread_percent, bid_size, ask_size,
  float) plus execution_tier (1-4, per item 13) computed from a combination of
  them, not raw share count alone. Market cap stays None (still no fundamentals
  source) and order-book depth beyond top-of-book bid/ask size isn't available
  from Alpaca's IEX feed — will be marked unavailable, not estimated.

  9. Position sizing × liquidity interaction

  participation_rate = position_shares / avg_volume (and separately / 
  relative-volume-adjusted volume where available), computed at configurable
  rates (0.1/0.5/1/2/5%, per item 4) — these become inputs a candidate is tested
  against, not a hardcoded assumption of which one is correct.

  10. Small-account simulation

  A dedicated account_sim.py runs the same signal through the same execution 
  engine at multiple starting_equity values ($100/$500/$1,000/$5,000/$10,000
  alongside the standardized $100,000 research baseline) — mechanically
  identical to what I already did manually for you two messages ago, just made a
  first-class, reusable, always-on part of the research output instead of a
  one-off script. Signal engine output never changes across these runs; only
  execution-engine verdicts do.

  ---

  Given the size of this, I'm going to build the foundational,
  correctness-critical pieces myself (the bearish signal definition, the
  provenance/timestamp model, the shortability design) and delegate the more
  mechanical-but-large execution/outcome/reporting layers to a strong agent,
  then verify everything myself and run a critique pass before reporting back —
  same pattern as the last overhaul. Starting now.

     scanned (not just Ross-passed ones) and dedupes by keeping each symbol's

     actually moved. So a stock that later legitimately passed at 2pm gets
     discovery-timestamped at 9:31am (when it hadn't moved yet), and the

     not a market finding.

     consolidated (SIP) data — it's IEX-only, structurally. That corroborates

     but the specific "~40x" figure is the agent's outside estimate, not
     something verified against this account — I'd treat that multiplier as
     approximate, not precise.

     finding here matches and extends what I'd already flagged.
